title: The Evening Brief: Injury fallout across four sports dims the landscape
dek: Aaron Judge and Lamar Jackson joined two college football starting quarterbacks in exiting their games with significant injuries Sunday. The baseball and football playoffs tip forward despite the absences.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: A single day saw four prominent starting quarterbacks or captains sidelined by injury, Judge ruled out of the ALDS, Jackson day-to-day after leaving a Ravens win, Heintschel lost for Pitt's season, and Brandon benched in Tennessee's game, reshaping lineups and starter questions across multiple leagues.
bottom_line: Judge's exclusion from the ALDS opens the Yankees' first-round series without their captain; Heintschel's season-ending ACL tear forces Pittsburgh to lean on backup Greiner against ranked ACC opponents; Jackson's ankle injury status will be tested by the Ravens' schedule; and Brandon's benching signals uncertainty about Tennessee's quarterback future. Game 2 of the Rays-Yankees ALDS is October 6 in Tampa Bay, Game 3 of the Brewers-Padres series is Tuesday in San Diego, and both will reveal whether the early injuries define the postseason or whether the absent players return to alter the trajectory.
body: Sunday brought a cascade of injuries that will reshape rosters and decision-making across baseball and football in the coming days. The thread is simple: availability collapsed for several prominent starters at precisely the moment playoff and conference play demands their presence.

The most significant absence is Aaron Judge's. The Yankees' captain and three-time AL MVP will not appear on the 26-man ALDS roster against Tampa Bay after his moderate right calf strain, sustained September 16, did not heal in time. Manager Aaron Boone said Judge wanted to play and was willing to serve as a late-inning option, but Boone determined he needed more recovery time. Judge remains eligible for a potential ALCS if the Yankees advance. The decision reflects the manager's caution in the first round rather than a permanent conclusion on Judge's postseason participation.

In the NFL, Lamar Jackson exited Baltimore's 24-18 victory over Tennessee late in the first half with an ankle injury and did not return. Head coach Jesse Minter has not determined the extent of the injury, and NFL Network reports Jackson is day-to-day. Tyler Huntley took over for the second half. The Ravens play Cincinnati on October 10; Jackson's status for that game depends on how the ankle responds in the coming days.

College football absorbed two concurrent quarterback losses. Pittsburgh's Mason Heintschel, who led the nation with 14 touchdown passes, suffered a season-ending ACL tear during the Panthers' 35-33 victory over Virginia Tech on Friday. Backup Holden Greiner took over and led Pittsburgh to victory, completing 8 of 12 passes for 78 yards and a touchdown. The 5-0 Panthers face North Carolina next Saturday without their leading scorer. Tennessee benched five-star freshman Faizon Brandon after one interception during the Auburn game, with backup George MacIntyre leading the Vols to victory. Brandon, the nation's No. 3 quarterback prospect, went three-for-eight before head coach Josh Heupel pulled him, citing that he "wasn't operating" and "didn't feel 100 percent." Whether Heupel returns Brandon to the starting job or gives the position to MacIntyre will signal the coaching staff's confidence level in the freshman's development.

On the field, the playoffs and high-stakes games proceeded. In the ALDS, Drew Rasmussen carried a no-hitter 7 2/3 innings as the Tampa Bay Rays defeated the Yankees 1-0 in Game 1, retiring 15 straight batters with a career-high 23 swinging strikes. Jonathan Aranda's third-inning home run provided the only run support. The Milwaukee Brewers took a 2-0 NLDS lead with a 4-3 walk-off victory over San Diego on Jackson Chourio's ninth-inning single. The Dallas Cowboys erased a 10-point halftime deficit to defeat the winless Houston Texans 34-30, with CeeDee Lamb catching a career-high 17 passes for 189 yards and the game-winning 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds remaining. Lamb was targeted on 21 of 45 routes, the most by any receiver running 45 or fewer routes in a single game since 2016. The Texans, now 0-4, have historical precedent to draw on: only the 1992 Chargers have made the playoffs after an 0-4 start.

In rugby league, Wakefield Trinity won the Super League Grand Final 27-14 over Warrington Wolves, claiming their first championship since 1968. The victory completes a two-year climb from Championship-level play to the sport's top prize.

Away from competition, the NFL suspended 49ers owner Jed York for six games and fined him $500,000 on Friday for violating the personal conduct policy following his August arrest in an Ohio prostitution sting. York, who has not attended games or league meetings this season and was credited with three games served, is eligible to return on October 20.
